column5: A fresh idempotency key is minted on every submit so the key cannot deduplicate a retry after a timeout
column6: handleCheckout at src/helpers/functionalHelpers.ts:463-568 reads state.checkout.idempotencyKey at :486 and sends it as idempotency_key at :491. Both submit paths dispatch setIdempotencyKey(genKey()) immediately before calling it - src/views/CartPageView/CheckoutSection.tsx:125 and src/components/Modals/PaymentModal.tsx:46 - so every attempt carries a different key and the server can never match two attempts. The comment at PaymentModal.tsx:43-45 shows this is deliberate: a new key lets a gateway switch create a fresh order and a double-tap is blocked by the disabled button. That reasoning holds for those two cases but not for the case idempotency keys exist for. When the request times out or the connection drops after the panel has already created the order the client sees a failure - the finally block at CheckoutSection.tsx:153-156 re-enables the button - and the next click generates a NEW key so the panel treats it as a new order.
column10: User places an order and the response is lost to a timeout or a dropped connection after the panel has committed the order.
column11: 1. Begin checkout and place an order. 2. Interrupt the response so the client records a failure while the server has already created the order - throttle to offline after the request leaves or force a gateway timeout. 3. Press place order again on the re-enabled button. 4. Compare the resulting orders in the account.
column12: The retry carries the same idempotency key so the panel recognises it and returns the original order instead of creating a second one.
column13: The retry carries a newly generated key so a second order is created for the same cart - and for a prepaid method a second payment intent follows it.
column14: Duplicate orders and potentially duplicate charges on exactly the failure mode the idempotency_key field was added to protect. The customer is billed twice and the seller ships twice.
column15: Keep one key per checkout attempt rather than per submit - generate it when the checkout is entered or when the cart contents change and regenerate it only when the payment method actually changes so the gateway-switch case in the PaymentModal comment still works. Clear it after a confirmed success in resetCheckOutState which already runs at functionalHelpers.ts:457.

column5: The wallet recharge amount is divided by 100 and multiplied by 100 again which yields a non-integer paise value for about 13 percent of amounts
column6: src/components/PaymentGateway/RazorPay.tsx builds the wallet order at :136-141 by dividing the server supplied paise amount by 100 at :138 - amount: walletOrderData.payment_response.amount / 100 - and then multiplies it straight back at :145 - amount: order.amount * 100 - when constructing the Razorpay options. The round trip is pointless because payment_response.amount is already the integer paise figure the gateway wants and it is lossy in IEEE754. Measured over every paise value between 1.00 and 10000.00 the expression returns a non-integer for 131248 of 999901 values which is 13.1 percent - the smallest failing case is 0.07 which yields 7.000000000000001 and everyday values fail too including 1.10 and 2.01 and 1.15. Razorpay requires an integer amount in the smallest currency unit. The order payment path at :200-204 does NOT have this defect - it passes pr.amount through untouched - so the correct pattern already exists in the same file.
column10: Wallet recharge through Razorpay for an amount whose paise value fails the round trip - roughly one value in eight.
column11: 1. Open the wallet recharge flow and choose Razorpay. 2. Enter an amount such as 1.10 or 2.01 whose paise value fails the round trip. 3. Inspect the amount passed into the Razorpay options object before checkout opens.
column12: The integer paise amount from the server is passed to the gateway unchanged exactly as the order path does at :200-204.
column13: A floating point value such as 110.00000000000001 is passed as the amount where the gateway requires an integer in the smallest currency unit.
column14: Wallet recharge can fail or mismatch against the server created order for a large share of amounts. Because it depends on the specific amount it will look intermittent and be hard to reproduce from a bug report.
column15: Delete the round trip and pass walletOrderData.payment_response.amount directly into options.amount. If a display value in major units is needed derive it separately and never feed it back into the gateway amount.

column5: Wallet recharge is declared successful from the client-side gateway callback with no server confirmation
column6: The wallet branch handler at src/components/PaymentGateway/RazorPay.tsx:149-157 runs onSuccess() and raises a Wallet Recharged Successfully toast as soon as the Razorpay checkout callback fires. Nothing is sent to the panel from that handler and no confirmation call is made - the callback signature at :149 is an argument-less async arrow so razorpay_payment_id and the signature that Razorpay hands to the handler are discarded rather than forwarded. The balance is only credited server side once the gateway webhook is processed so the toast asserts an outcome the storefront has not verified. The order path at :205-208 has the same shape but is materially safer because it only flips local UI state and the order status is re-read from the panel afterwards.
column10: Wallet recharge completed in the Razorpay modal while the webhook is delayed - or a webhook that fails or never arrives.
column11: 1. Recharge the wallet through Razorpay and complete payment. 2. Read the success toast. 3. Immediately open the wallet balance before the webhook has been processed.
column12: Success is confirmed against the panel - either by posting the gateway payment reference for verification or by re-reading the wallet balance before the success state is shown.
column13: The success toast appears immediately on the client callback and the balance can still be unchanged behind it.
column14: Customer is told the wallet is recharged while the balance says otherwise which drives support contacts and repeat recharge attempts. If a webhook is lost entirely the customer keeps a success message for money that was never credited.
column15: Forward the Razorpay payment reference from the handler to a panel verification endpoint and show success only on its confirmation - or poll the wallet balance once before switching to the success state. Report the pending case honestly instead of asserting success.

column5: All five payment gateway components raise hard-coded English strings to the user
column6: None of the components under src/components/PaymentGateway/ route their user-facing strings through i18n. RazorPay.tsx carries the most with strings including Invalid wallet order data at :129 - Wallet Recharged Successfully! at :153 - Payment Cancelled and You have closed the Razorpay checkout. at :168-169 - Failed to start payment at :188 and the gateway descriptions Wallet Recharge at :147 and Pay Safe at :203. Paystack.tsx - BankTransfer.tsx - Stripe.tsx and FlutterwavePayment.tsx follow the same pattern. CLAUDE.md section 6.6 requires every user-facing string to come from t('namespace.key') with the key present in en - hi and ar. The surrounding checkout code already complies - CheckoutSection.tsx uses t() for its toasts at :118 and :133 - so the payment layer is the outlier.
column10: Application language set to Hindi or Arabic. Any payment attempt or cancellation.
column11: 1. Switch the language to Arabic or Hindi. 2. Start a payment and then dismiss the gateway modal. 3. Read the toast.
column12: The message renders in the active language from the locale bundles like the rest of the checkout flow.
column13: Every payment gateway message renders in English whatever the language is set to.
column14: Hindi and Arabic customers meet untranslated English at the payment step which is the highest value and least forgiving moment in the funnel. Arabic users also get left-to-right English inside an otherwise right-to-left page.
column15: Move every user-facing string in the five gateway components into the locale bundles under a payment namespace - add the keys to en hi and ar - and run npm run scan:i18n. Cover the ondismiss and error paths as well as the success paths.
